html:
SMTO-CFG-0076 — Task Contract size settings don't fit together

GUID: 243174b1-fbcb-4dab-a0fb-df615ff9e560
Slug: task-contract-token-policy-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • A Task Contract is the step-by-step brief SMTO writes from your request before the Agent starts. Its size, thinking and retry numbers don't fit within the allowed limits, so SMTO didn't accept them.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Agent behavior › Task Contracts. Use 1,024–65,536 for Task Contract maximum output tokens, 3–10 Automatic retries, and a multiple of 256 up to 8,192 for Token increase per retry. Each number must stay inside its own allowed range.
  2. If Automatic Task Contract recovery is on, make sure maximum output tokens plus Automatic retries times Token increase per retry is 65,536 or less, for example 8,192 + 3 × 1,024 = 11,264. The last retry asks for the most room, and that can't go past 65,536.
  3. If Task Contract thinking is set to Bounded budget, make Task Contract thinking budget a multiple of 128 and smaller than Task Contract maximum output tokens. The brief itself needs room left over after thinking.
  4. If this appeared when you lowered Maximum completion tokens in Settings › Setup › Model routing, reduce the Task Contract numbers first, then lower it. That general limit must stay large enough for the biggest Task Contract attempt.

What success looks like

  • The Task Contracts section saves without an error, and new tasks start normally.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Change only the Task Contract numbers described here; don't raise unrelated timeouts or budgets. Tasks already running keep the numbers they started with.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Task Contract compiler policy failed validation: a field is outside its type, range or step, the thinking budget is not below the initial output cap, the largest enabled retry exceeds 65,536 tokens, or llm_max_tokens was lowered below the required headroom.

What this means

  • Task-contract generation policy fails enum/boolean/integer/step bounds, allocates thinking at least its initial output cap, exceeds 65,536 at its largest enabled retry, or lowers the general cap below required headroom. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Task-contract generation policy fails enum/boolean/integer/step bounds, allocates thinking at least its initial output cap, exceeds 65,536 at its largest enabled retry, or lowers the general cap below required headroom.

How to diagnose it

  • Check each named compiler setting and compute initial output plus enabled retry increments; retry index and general model ceilings are separate constraints.

How to fix it

  • Correct task_contract_max_tokens (1,024–65,536), task_contract_auto_recovery_retries (3–10), task_contract_auto_recovery_increment_tokens (256–8,192, step 256), task_contract_thinking_mode, and task_contract_thinking_budget_tokens (128–32,768, step 128, below max_tokens in budget mode), keeping max_tokens + retries × increment ≤ 65,536 and llm_max_tokens at or above that amount. Changes apply to new tasks; existing runs keep their captured policy.
  • Correct the specific compiler field or coupled token bound, keeping thinking below its initial output allowance and the largest attempt within 65,536.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The normalized compiler policy fits all field bounds and required output headroom.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
